title: The Iron Wall: Odessa, the Legion, and the Order to Bring Him Home
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Odessa, birth on the Black Sea coast
stops.date_confidence: attested (English Wikipedia). Coordinates are the city centre; no fetched source gives a birth address.
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of October a son is born to Yevgeny Zhabotinsky and his wife in Odessa, the Black Sea port the Russian Empire built to be cosmopolitan and that its Jews made literate. They name him Vladimir; the Hebrew name Ze'ev, wolf, travels alongside it. Odessa in these years is grain brokers, Italian opera, Greek shipping agents, and a quarter of a million Jews who are neither shtetl nor gentry. He will spend his life explaining a nation to itself in the language of the empire that owned it. At home there is no Hebrew and no Yiddish; the family speaks Russian and reads Russian.
stops.quote_source: A childhood exchange reported in Shmuel Katz, Jabotinsky: A Life (Rebel and Statesman), in Katz's own third-person narration, not in Jabotinsky's memoir
suggested_refs: Jabotinsky's Russian memoir, published in English as Vladimir Jabotinsky's Story of My Life, ed. Horowitz and Katsis (Wayne State University Press, 2015)

stops.name: Odessa, the father's death
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the year 1886 comes from the dossier and was not independently confirmed in this pass; month and day unknown and defaulted. The tradition of an affluent early childhood could not be checked against it.
stops.campa: His father dies when the boy is five, a merchant of the Dnieper grain trade whose accounts do not survive him. The household drops out of comfort. One line of the dead man is preserved: told that an employee was stealing from him, he answered that the thief was poorer than he was and might have a right to what he took. The son grows up inside the reduced version of that generosity, a widow's economy in a boom city, and builds in adulthood a movement whose first principle is that no Jew should depend on another man's mercy. Whether the household had ever been as comfortable as the tradition says, no source in reach confirms.
stops.quote: He who steals from me is poorer than I, and maybe he has a right to what he takes.
stops.quote_source: Yona Jabotinsky, the father, quoted in Shmuel Katz, Rebel and Statesman
sources: dossier lead on the 1886 death, unconfirmed independently

stops.name: Bern, the first speech
stops.date_confidence: attested that he passed through Bern in 1898 as a teenage correspondent (Wikipedia). The speech and its content are Katz's report, in reported past tense, not a transcript; month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: Seventeen years old, sent abroad as correspondent for an Odessa paper, he stops in Bern among the Russian student colonies where every doctrine of the coming century is being argued in rented rooms. He gets up to speak in public for the first time. He holds no card, belongs to no faction, and has not yet met a Zionist organization. No transcript exists, and his biographer gives the content rather than the words: what he told the room, Katz writes, was that the Jews of the Diaspora were facing a St. Bartholomew's Night.
suggested_refs: Katz, Rebel and Statesman, on the Berne address at seventeen

stops.name: Rome, the law student called Altalena
stops.date_confidence: attested: registered at the University of Rome from autumn 1898, attending irregularly for about three years, never graduating (Wikipedia). The pin is the historic Sapienza seat on Corso del Rinascimento; the exact building is not confirmed by a fetched source.
stops.campa: He registers in the autumn as a law student at the University of Rome and attends when it suits him, which is seldom. Italy gives him what Odessa could not: Garibaldi read as scripture, Mazzini's nation as an act of will, an opera house sense of how a people announces itself. He files feuilletons home to Russian papers under the pen name Altalena, the swing, chosen because it moves. Three years pass this way. He takes no degree and will call Italy his spiritual homeland for the rest of his life.
stops.quote: Exactness of dates is of no interest to me; I do not remember them and I have no time to dig for them
stops.quote_source: Jabotinsky, letter to his sister, quoted in Shmuel Katz, Rebel and Statesman
suggested_refs: The Palazzo della Sapienza, historic seat of the University of Rome

stops.name: Odessa, two months in isolation
stops.date_confidence: attested as an arrest for anti-establishment feuilletons with roughly two months' detention (Wikipedia); the April dating and the association with a radical Italian publication are dossier leads not independently confirmed. Day defaulted.
stops.campa: The tsarist police arrest him in the spring for the anti-establishment feuilletons and for what he has been printing abroad, and hold him roughly two months, much of it in isolation. Prison is a normal stage in the education of a Russian writer; he comes out with the standing of a man the authorities have already troubled to notice. In the cell his thinking turns from copy to organization: not what a Jewish writer should say to Russia, but what Russian Jews should have ready the next time a crowd forms in the street outside.
sources: dossier lead on the April 1902 dating, unconfirmed

stops.name: Odessa, the self-defense organization
stops.date_confidence: attested, and the usual sequence is inverted: English Wikipedia states he joined the Zionist movement and established the Jewish Self-Defense Organization PRIOR to the Kishinev pogrom of April 1903. Dated to early 1903 to preserve that order; month and day unknown.
stops.campa: Before the Kishinev pogrom, not after it, he joins the Zionist movement and helps set up a Jewish self-defense organization in Odessa: young men, sticks, revolvers where revolvers can be got, lists of streets and courtyards. He is twenty-two, and until this year he has spent his adult life writing feuilletons about the Italian theatre. The sequence is usually told backward, as though the atrocity made the politics. When the news comes in April from Kishinev, forty-nine dead and the police standing by, it does not create his politics; it confirms them.
suggested_refs: The Jewish Self-Defense Organization of Odessa, 1903

stops.name: Basel, the Sixth Congress and Herzl's last
stops.date_confidence: attested: elected a Russian delegate to the Sixth Zionist Congress, the last Herzl attended, and opposed the Uganda scheme (Wikipedia). Day defaulted. The pin is the atlas's Stadtcasino coordinate; the venue for the 1903 congress specifically is not confirmed by a fetched source.
stops.campa: Elected a Russian delegate, he comes to Basel for the Sixth Zionist Congress and sees Theodor Herzl in the hall, the only time he ever will. The Congress is torn over the British offer of territory in East Africa, and the Russian delegates, whose own towns are being burned that same season, refuse a refuge that is not Palestine. Jabotinsky is with them, and will argue for forty years afterward that a shelter and a country are not two versions of one offer. Herzl is dead within the year, at forty-four.
suggested_refs: The Stadtcasino Basel, hall of the early Zionist Congresses

stops.name: Odessa, translating the city of slaughter
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction on the dating: the dossier put the translation in 1903, which is too early. Bialik's poem dates from 1903-04; Encyclopaedia Judaica records that Jabotinsky's Russian translation of Bialik's Songs and Poems was published in 1910 and became a bestseller. Composition dated here to c.1904 to order the segment.
stops.campa: Bialik goes to Kishinev to take testimony and comes back with a poem that curses the survivors for hiding in cellars while their women were raped. Jabotinsky puts it into Russian, and the Russian is what the assimilated readers of the empire actually read. The translation moves through student rooms in Odessa, Kiev, and St. Petersburg and recruits for self-defense better than any pamphlet does. The collected Bialik translations, published in 1910, sell like a novel.
suggested_refs: Hayim Nahman Bialik, In the City of Slaughter (1903-04), in Jabotinsky's Russian version
sources: dossier lead on the translation, redated

stops.name: St. Petersburg, Yevreiskaya Zhizn
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1904 (Wikipedia); month and day unknown and defaulted. Placed after the Basel stop in travel order although both carry the same defaulted date.
stops.campa: He moves north to the imperial capital to co-edit the Zionist weekly Yevreiskaya Zhizn, Jewish Life, arguing the case in Russian to Russian Jews who have spent a generation trying to become Russians. The censors read him; so do the students. It is one of several papers he will edit in five languages and four empires, and the first in which he writes for a movement rather than for himself. The method is fixed by now and never changes: no theology, no sentiment, a political argument delivered in the majority language, at speed, in public.
suggested_refs: Yevreiskaya Zhizn (Jewish Life), St. Petersburg

stops.name: Helsingfors, the program of the present
stops.date_confidence: attested: chief speaker at the Third All-Russian Conference of Zionists, November 1906 (Wikipedia); day defaulted.
stops.campa: At the Third All-Russian Conference of Zionists in Helsingfors he is the chief speaker, and the program that comes out of the hall is called Gegenwartsarbeit, work in the present. It commits Zionists to demand civil and national rights for Jews inside Russia now, in the same breath in which they build in Palestine. There is nothing quietist in it. The reasoning is that a people which cannot defend its rights in the empire it lives in will not know how to hold a country of its own once it has one.
suggested_refs: The Helsingfors Programme of 1906

stops.name: Odessa, marriage to Johanna Galperina
stops.date_confidence: attested for October 1907 (Wikipedia); day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: In October he marries Johanna Galperina, whom he has known in Odessa since they were both young. She follows him to Constantinople, to London, to Paris, to Jerusalem and to New York; she is widowed at a summer camp in the Catskills, buried on Long Island, and moved to Jerusalem when he is moved. Of the thousands of pages he wrote about the fate of nations, almost none are about her. What she thought of any of it, no source in this pool records, and the thinness of the record is on his side.

stops.name: Constantinople, Le Jeune Turc
stops.date_confidence: attested for the period 1908-1914 (Wikipedia); the specific year 1909 and the Pera location are chosen to order the segment and are not fixed by a fetched source.
stops.campa: The Young Turk revolution opens the Ottoman capital to newspapers and to people who want something from an empire in mid-repair. He settles in Pera, edits Le Jeune Turc, and runs Zionist press and information work aimed at Ottoman opinion, on the reasoning that the landlord of Palestine lives in this city and can be argued with. The reasoning fails. Within six years the same government deports the Jews of Jaffa, and he meets them again in Alexandria, in a refugee camp.
suggested_refs: Le Jeune Turc, Constantinople

stops.name: Odessa, the birth of Eri
stops.date_confidence: attested: English Wikipedia, 'Eri Jabotinsky', gives 26 December 1910 at Odessa. The dossier's 16 December is wrong by ten days. Knesset service confirmed: Herut, 1949-51.
stops.campa: His son is born in Odessa the day after Christmas and named Eri Theodore, the second name for Herzl. The boy grows up inside the movement his father is inventing, runs Revisionist immigration operations, is jailed by the British, and sits in the first Knesset of a state his father did not live to see. Johanna raises him in whichever city the politics has chosen that year, and the addresses go on changing: Odessa, Rome, St. Petersburg, Constantinople, and after them London, Paris, Jerusalem, New York. Jabotinsky is thirty.

stops.name: Alexandria, the refugees and Trumpeldor
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1915 (Wikipedia, 'Zion Mule Corps'); month and day defaulted. The coordinate is English Wikipedia's point for the city of Alexandria and is NOT the Gabbari refugee camp, which could not be separately sourced; the stop is therefore named for the city.
stops.campa: Some twelve hundred Jews expelled from Ottoman Palestine are camped in Alexandria under British administration, and he arrives among them as a war correspondent and stops being one. Here he meets Joseph Trumpeldor, one-armed, decorated by the Russians at Port Arthur. Together they put to General Maxwell a proposal for a Jewish fighting unit under its own flag. Maxwell offers transport duty at Gallipoli instead. Trumpeldor takes it and forms the Zion Mule Corps; Jabotinsky refuses and leaves for London to get the fighting battalion.
stops.quote: The only conditional demand was that Jews should be allowed to fight as Jews; that it should be recorded in the annals of this war that the Jews were one of the peoples fighting for the common good cause.
stops.quote_source: Jabotinsky, The War and the Jew (New York: Altalena Press, 1942), published after his death
suggested_refs: The Zion Mule Corps at Gallipoli, 1915
sources: Jabotinsky, The War and the Jew (1942), archive.org/details/warandthejew009960mbp

stops.name: London, the East End and the private's uniform
stops.date_confidence: attested: enlisted as a private in the 20th Battalion, London Regiment, January 1917 (Wikipedia); day defaulted. The East End recruiting figure of roughly 30,000 refugees is from the same source.
stops.campa: For two years he works the East End, some thirty thousand Russian Jewish refugees who are not British subjects, not conscriptable, and not enthusiastic about dying for an empire whose cousins turned their grandparents away. They heckle him. Some of them beat him. He lobbies the War Cabinet through Leo Amery and through Colonel Patterson, and in January he enlists as a private in the 20th Battalion of the London Regiment, so as to stop being a man who asks other men to enlist. In November the Balfour Declaration is published and the battalions follow.
suggested_refs: The Balfour Declaration, 2 November 1917
arthur_balfour.journey.json

stops.name: Umm al-Shert, the bridge in the Jordan Valley
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'Jewish Legion'). Coordinates are approximate for the Jordan Valley crossing and do not correspond to a precisely fixed modern landmark.
stops.campa: In the Jordan Valley the 38th Battalion of the Royal Fusiliers is ordered to take the only bridge in the sector. Patterson sends a company forward; it is thrown back with casualties. He sends the second company, under Lieutenant Jabotinsky, and the crossing is taken. Whatever else the Jewish Legion is on paper, at this hour it is a unit with an objective on a military map, and men whose great-grandfathers were forbidden to carry a weapon are holding a bridge over the Jordan. Patterson writes the action up afterward in his own account of the campaign. The date is the twenty-second of September, 1918.
suggested_refs: Lt.-Col. J. H. Patterson, With the Judaeans in the Palestine Campaign

stops.name: As-Salt, the garrison in Gilead
stops.date_confidence: attested to September 1918 (Wikipedia, 'Jewish Legion'); the exact day is not fixed by the source and the 25th is set to follow the bridge action in order.
stops.campa: The battalion crosses east of the Jordan into Gilead and garrisons As-Salt, a hill town of stone houses above the Balqa plain. The war ends around them there. Measured against the Palestine campaign as a whole what they have done is small: a bridge, a garrison, a season of malaria. It is also the documented fact he wanted, Jewish soldiers under a Jewish flag inside the British order of battle, which no later negotiation could pretend had never occurred. The sick lists that autumn are longer than the casualty lists.
suggested_refs: The 38th Battalion, Royal Fusiliers, at As-Salt

stops.name: Jerusalem, out of uniform and into the Order
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the September 1919 demobilization after criticizing the reduction of the Legion, and the December 1919 MBE, are dossier leads not independently confirmed in this pass. The pin is the atlas's canonical Jerusalem coordinate, inherited byte-identical; his precise location at demobilization is not established.
stops.campa: The British run the Jewish battalions down through the year, discharging men and refusing replacements, and he says so in public, which ends his service. He is demobilized in September. In December the Crown appoints him Member of the Order of the British Empire for the same war. He is thirty-nine, out of uniform for good, and keeps the decoration and the grievance in the same drawer. Within four months the government that decorated him will sentence him to fifteen years' hard labour.
sources: dossier leads on the demobilization and the MBE, unconfirmed independently

stops.name: Jerusalem, six hundred men drilling
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, '1920 Nebi Musa riots'): by late March about 600 volunteers were training daily. Day defaulted. Pin is the canonical Jerusalem coordinate; the geography lens placed the drilling near Jaffa Gate at 31.7767/35.2286.
stops.campa: With Pinhas Rutenberg he organizes a self-defense network in Jerusalem and takes no trouble to hide it. By late March some six hundred volunteers drill daily: calisthenics, stick fighting, the handling of whatever weapons the group can produce. The military administration knows, and he intends it to know. The argument, made to British officers to their faces, is that a government which cannot guarantee the safety of a quarter has no standing to forbid that quarter to guarantee its own.

stops.name: Jerusalem, the pistol and the arrest
stops.date_confidence: attested: arrested 6 April 1920 during the Palestine riots (Wikipedia). Pin is the canonical Jerusalem coordinate rather than the Old City point.
stops.campa: The Nabi Musa pilgrimage turns into days of killing inside the Old City walls. The military governor, Ronald Storrs, confiscates his pistol; the army keeps his drilled volunteers outside the walls through most of it. When it is over he does not wait to be collected. He presents himself for arrest as the commander of the defense group, rather than let the men be taken one at a time, and nineteen of them are taken with him anyway. The charge sheet names illegal possession of arms and the organization of an armed force.
suggested_refs: The Nebi Musa riots of April 1920

stops.name: Acre, fifteen years in the citadel
stops.date_confidence: attested for the conviction, the fifteen-year sentence, and the July 1920 amnesty (Wikipedia). Month and day of the transfer to Acre defaulted. The pin is the Ottoman citadel on the old-city peninsula, approximated; Wikipedia's coordinate for Acre (32.9278/35.0817) is the modern town centre roughly 1.2 km east and would misplace the prison.
stops.campa: A British military court gives him fifteen years' hard labour for illegal possession of arms and for organizing an armed force, and he is sent by way of Egypt to the Ottoman fort at Acre that the Mandate uses as a prison. The sentence raises an uproar from London to New York. General Congreve cuts it to one year; in July the High Commissioner, Herbert Samuel, amnesties everyone convicted over the riots, Jew and Arab alike. Yaakov Ben-Dov films the nineteen prisoners in the courtyard. Three minutes, silent.
suggested_refs: The Ben-Dov film of the Acre prisoners, 1920, held by the Jerusalem Cinematheque / Jewish Film Archive
sources: Jabotinsky Institute holdings as reported in the dossier, unverified (en.jabotinsky.org returns HTTP 403)

stops.name: London, Keren Hayesod
stops.date_confidence: attested: Keren Hayesod established at the World Zionist Congress in London, 7-24 July 1920, with Weizmann, Einstein and Jabotinsky among its early leaders (Wikipedia, 'Keren Hayesod'). The dossier's 1921 date for the fund is wrong by a year; 1921 belongs to his joining the Zionist Executive.
stops.campa: The World Zionist Congress meeting in London through July establishes Keren Hayesod, the foundation fund that will buy the land and pay for the settlement and the immigration, and he is among its first leaders alongside Chaim Weizmann and Albert Einstein. The next year Weizmann brings him onto the Zionist Executive and puts him in charge of information work. For two years the sharpest critic of the Zionist establishment sits inside it, drafting its propaganda and traveling for its money and learning exactly how slow it means to be. He stays until January 1923.
suggested_refs: Keren Hayesod, founded July 1920
einstein.journey.json

stops.name: Paris, the gendarmerie that never formed
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the Slavynsky negotiation is a dossier lead, unconfirmed independently in this pass; month and day unknown and defaulted. The pin is the atlas's canonical Paris coordinate, inherited byte-identical; the negotiations were conducted in exile diplomacy and not fixed to one city by the sources.
stops.campa: Through Maksym Slavynsky, envoy of Symon Petliura's Ukrainian government in exile, he negotiates an agreement for a Jewish gendarmerie to accompany a projected Ukrainian army and protect Jewish towns from the pogroms that army's own units had been carrying out. No gendarmerie is ever formed. The Jewish world attacks him for taking the hand of a man whose soldiers had killed tens of thousands of Jews. His answer is that he would negotiate with anyone capable of stopping the next massacre. Whether that government could have stopped anything, holding no territory and no army it could discipline, is a question the record never had to answer.
sources: dossier lead on the Slavynsky agreement, unconfirmed independently

stops.name: London, the resignation from the Executive
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the precise date of 18 January 1923 is a dossier lead not independently confirmed; the 1923 break with mainstream Zionism is attested (Wikipedia).
stops.campa: In January he resigns from the Zionist Executive, and for a time from the Zionist Organization altogether. The quarrel is about pace and about naming. He wants the Jewish state declared as the open objective rather than implied in careful English; he wants both banks of the Jordan held to the Mandate's original text; he does not believe the British will deliver a country they are already dividing. Weizmann's method is patience and good relations with the men who hold the pen. Jabotinsky walks out and begins building a second Zionism outside the room.
sources: dossier lead on the exact date, unconfirmed

stops.name: Riga, the founding of Betar
stops.date_confidence: attested that his Riga visit led young Latvian activists to found Betar in 1923, with Aharon Propes arranging the meeting (Wikipedia, 'Betar'). Month and day unknown and defaulted; the founding itself falls later in the year than this ordering date.
stops.campa: He speaks to a hall of Jewish schoolboys and students in Riga, at a meeting arranged by a young activist named Aharon Propes, and what the boys take away is not an argument but a form: uniform, rank, drill, Hebrew, and the name of Joseph Trumpeldor, three years dead at Tel Hai. They found Brit Yosef Trumpeldor, Betar, that year. Within a decade the movement has tens of thousands of members across Poland, Latvia, and Lithuania. Most of them are murdered before they turn thirty.
suggested_refs: Betar (Brit Yosef Trumpeldor), founded at Riga, 1923

stops.name: Berlin, the iron wall
stops.date_confidence: the essay's publication in Rassvet on 4 November 1923 is attested by the primary text transcription; his residence in Berlin in 1923-25 while editing Rassvet is a dossier claim not confirmed by a fetched source, and Rassvet's editorial base moved between Berlin and Paris.
stops.campa: In November he publishes in Rassvet the essay that becomes the doctrine of everything after it. Its argument is not that the Arabs of Palestine are a rabble to be bought off; it is the reverse. They are a living nation who love the country as any nation loves its own and will therefore never agree to being settled over. Since they will not agree, settlement can proceed only behind a force they cannot break, and the settlers should stop lying to the Arabs and to themselves about what it is they are doing.
stops.quote: Every indigenous people will resist alien settlers as long as they see any hope of ridding themselves of the danger of foreign settlement.
stops.quote_source: Jabotinsky, The Iron Wall (We and the Arabs), Rassvet, 4 November 1923, English text at marxists.org/history/etol/document/mideast/ironwall/ironwall.htm
suggested_refs: Jabotinsky, The Iron Wall (We and the Arabs), 1923
sources: Jabotinsky, The Iron Wall (1923), marxists.org transcription (fetched)
dossier lead on the Berlin residence, unconfirmed

stops.name: Berlin, the ethics of the iron wall
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the existence of an ethical sequel published in Rassvet within days is a dossier lead; the quoted sentence is verified in the primary English text of the Iron Wall material. The 11 November date orders the pair and is not independently confirmed.
stops.campa: He prints the sequel, in which the wall is not the end of the argument but its precondition. Only when no crack shows in it, he writes, will the extreme groups lose their following and the moderates be able to negotiate terms a Jewish majority could accept. For the next century each half is quoted by a different party: the wall by his heirs, the settlement by his opponents. He set the two halves down within a week of each other, in the same paper, over the same signature.
stops.quote: Only when not a single breach is visible in the iron wall, only then do extreme groups lose their sway, and influence transfers to moderate groups.
stops.quote_source: Jabotinsky, The Iron Wall (1923), English text at marxists.org/history/etol/document/mideast/ironwall/ironwall.htm
suggested_refs: Jabotinsky, The Ethics of the Iron Wall, Rassvet, November 1923
sources: Jabotinsky, The Iron Wall (1923), marxists.org transcription (fetched)

stops.name: Paris, the Union of Zionists-Revisionists
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1925 by Encyclopaedia Judaica and Wikipedia, 'Revisionist Zionism'; the dossier collapsed the 1923 break and the 1925 founding into one event and they are separated here. Month and day are not fixed by the sources. Canonical Paris pin.
stops.campa: A convention of his followers in Paris proclaims the World Union of Zionists-Revisionists. Revision means a return to the Mandate as it was originally written and to Herzl's declared aim, stated out loud. The program is a Jewish majority on both banks of the Jordan, immigration organized as an evacuation rather than a trickle, and a Jewish army. Under all of it runs a liberal individualism his enemies never credit him with and his own movement steadily forgets. Every man is a king, he writes, meaning the individual against the state and not rank of any kind.
stops.quote_source: Jabotinsky, On State and Social Problems, p. 52, quoted in Kremnitzer and Fuchs, Ze'ev Jabotinsky on Democracy, Equality, and Individual Rights (Israel Democracy Institute, 2013)
suggested_refs: Kremnitzer and Fuchs, Ze'ev Jabotinsky on Democracy, Equality, and Individual Rights (IDI, 2013), en.idi.org.il/media/6745/jabotinsky-idi-2013.pdf
sources: Kremnitzer and Fuchs (IDI, 2013), PDF fetched and text-extracted

stops.name: Jerusalem, Do'ar HaYom and the closing of the country
stops.date_confidence: attested: he took the editorship of Do'ar HaYom from Itamar Ben-Avi in 1928 and was barred from returning after leaving in 1930 (Wikipedia, 'Do'ar HaYom' and 'Ze'ev Jabotinsky'). Month and day unknown. Pin is the canonical Jerusalem coordinate: the geography lens gave 31.7807/35.2258 for the HaSolel Street office, which is about 600 m off the actual street and was rejected rather than shipped.
stops.campa: He takes over the Hebrew daily Do'ar HaYom from its founder Itamar Ben-Avi and edits it from the offices on HaSolel Street, living in Palestine for the first time as a resident rather than as a soldier or a prisoner. It lasts about two years. He goes abroad in 1930 on a lecture tour, and the Colonial Office, with the riots of August 1929 behind it and no appetite for him at all, declines to let him back in. He is fifty years old. He never sees the country again.
suggested_refs: Do'ar HaYom, Jerusalem

stops.name: Danzig, elected Rosh Betar
stops.date_confidence: attested: elected Rosh Betar at the movement's first world conference in Danzig, 1931 (Wikipedia, 'Betar'). The dossier's 1929 date and its 'unspecified' place are both wrong. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: At Betar's first world conference, held in the Free City of Danzig, he is elected Rosh Betar, head of the movement, and the organization takes its final shape under him: hadar, a code of bearing and self-command; Hebrew; military training; a doctrine of the Jew who does not flinch. Danzig in 1931 is a German-speaking port under League of Nations administration, and the boys drilling in its halls are being trained for a country that does not exist. He has been forbidden to enter that country since the previous year.
suggested_refs: The first world conference of Betar, Danzig, 1931

stops.name: Paris, the Arlosoroff defense
stops.date_confidence: the shooting on 16 June 1933 and the arrests are dossier leads not independently confirmed in this pass. The killing and the trial are Tel Aviv events at which Jabotinsky, barred from Palestine since 1930, was not present; the pin is the canonical Paris coordinate standing for the movement's European base, and his own whereabouts on the day are not established by any source in this pool.
stops.campa: Haim Arlosoroff, political head of the Jewish Agency, is shot dead walking on the Tel Aviv beach with his wife. Within days three Revisionists are arrested and the Labour press declares the whole movement a murder gang. Jabotinsky, who cannot enter the country, runs the defense from Europe: lawyers, money, a campaign in every language he writes in. Stavsky is convicted and then acquitted on appeal for want of a second witness. The murder is never solved. The accusation is never withdrawn.
suggested_refs: The Arlosoroff case, Tel Aviv, 1933
sources: dossier lead on the Arlosoroff affair, unconfirmed independently

stops.name: London, the meetings with Ben-Gurion
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the Rutenberg-brokered London meetings, the signed agreements, and the Histadrut referendum that rejected them are widely reported in the biographical literature but were not confirmed against a fetched source in this pass. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: The industrialist Pinhas Rutenberg gets the two men into the same room in London and they stay at it for weeks. Jabotinsky's people are being kept out of the labour exchanges and beaten at the docks. They sign agreements to end the violence between the movements and to regulate labour disputes, and each of them privately finds the other a serious man. The Histadrut membership then votes the accords down in a referendum. In print, before the meetings, David Ben-Gurion had called him Vladimir Hitler.
suggested_refs: The Jabotinsky-Ben-Gurion agreements of 1934 and the Histadrut referendum of 1935
sources: dossier lead on the London meetings, unconfirmed independently
QUEUE.md, Ze'ev Jabotinsky entry (the rivalry as framed for the atlas)

stops.name: Civitavecchia, the naval academy
stops.date_confidence: the existence of the Betar naval academy is attested (Wikipedia, 'Betar'), which gives neither its location nor a date; Civitavecchia, 1934, and Halpern's role are dossier leads. NO source, fetched or otherwise, places Jabotinsky himself at Civitavecchia: the stop is his movement's institution at its own port, not a visit of his.
stops.campa: Fascist Italy lets the Revisionists open a naval academy at Civitavecchia, the port of Rome, and Betar cadets learn seamanship in Italian uniforms under an Italian institutional roof. Jeremiah Halpern runs it on the ground. Jabotinsky, who has spent a decade courting Mussolini's government on the principle that a movement without a state must borrow whatever patron it can find, is not recorded as ever setting foot on the quay. In 1938 the Italian racial laws close the school and end the courtship together. The cadets go home.

stops.name: Vienna, the Konzerthaus congress
stops.date_confidence: attested: the founding congress of the New Zionist Organization drew 310 delegates from 34 countries and elected him president (Wikipedia, 'New Zionist Organization'); day defaulted.
stops.campa: Three hundred and ten delegates from thirty-four countries meet in Vienna, constitute the New Zionist Organization, elect him its president, and make the split final. He now commands a movement, a youth army, a press in six languages, and a naval school, and holds no seat at any table where the future of Palestine is actually being decided. What he does not have is time. He says so constantly, to audiences who mostly hear a man shouting. He is fifty-five years old.

segments.name: Poland, and the Novel of Odessa

stops.name: Warsaw, the evacuation plan
stops.date_confidence: attested that he solicited Polish government support for an evacuation plan (Wikipedia); the figure of 1.5 million over ten years and the dealings with Foreign Minister Beck are dossier leads. Begin's headship of Betar in Poland is dated 1937 by English Wikipedia and March 1939 by the dossier, and no fetched source says Jabotinsky personally appointed him; the conflict is left open.
stops.campa: He puts to the Polish government a plan to move a million and a half Jews out of Europe to Palestine within ten years, and Warsaw listens for its own reasons: Colonel Beck's foreign ministry would prefer fewer Jews and is willing to fund and arm Betar and the Irgun toward that end. Jewish Poland hears the word evacuation and recoils, hearing the antisemites' own program in a Jewish mouth. He is asking three million people to give up a thousand years of settlement on the strength of a forecast. Menachem Begin takes over the Polish branch, the largest in the world.
suggested_refs: The Evacuation Plan and the Polish arms and training given to Betar and the Irgun

stops.name: Paris, the five children of Odessa
stops.date_confidence: attested for the novel's 1936 Russian publication, the 1960 first substantial critical essay (Margolin), and the 2005 Cornell English translation by Michael R. Katz (Barry P. Scherr, Slavic Review). Month and day unknown; the Paris pin is the canonical atlas coordinate and the place of publication.
stops.campa: In the middle of the political years he publishes a novel in Russian about five children of one assimilated Jewish family in the Odessa of his own youth, each destroyed in a different way: apostasy, prison, suicide, the police, the sea. It is the least didactic thing he ever wrote and the only one with no program in it. Almost nobody reviews it. The first substantial essay on it appears in 1960, the first English translation in 2005, sixty-nine years after the book.

stops.name: Warsaw, the speech that may not have been given
stops.date_confidence: DISPUTED and left unresolved. Tradition places the volcano speech on Tisha B'Av 1938 in Warsaw. A 2023 study by Goldstein and Huri, reported in English Wikipedia, concludes that he never made the speech, that the published text differs from what he said, and that the prophetic wording may have been fabricated in 1958 in support of the reburial campaign. Month set to August for the fast; day defaulted.
stops.campa: On the fast of the Ninth of Av, tradition holds, he stands in Warsaw and tells Polish Jewry that they are living on the rim of a volcano about to pour out all-consuming lava, and that they must get out while getting out is still permitted. The passage is read aloud at Israeli memorial ceremonies every year as prophecy fulfilled. In 2023 archival researchers reported that the words appear in no contemporaneous record, that the printed text does not match what was said, and that the prophetic wording looks to have been composed in 1958, to help bring his body home. What he said in Warsaw that day, if he spoke at all, is not established.
suggested_refs: Goldstein and Huri (2023), on the fabrication of the Warsaw prophecy
sources: the dossier's own caution on the speech, retained

stops.name: Paris, the forecast of March 1939
stops.date_confidence: the passage is dated March 1939 by the Jewish Review of Books, which names no original outlet, so it is traceable only to a secondary source and no primary document has been located. The Jewish Review of Books prints it as a bracketed mid-sentence excerpt. His own whereabouts in March 1939 are not established; the pin is the canonical Paris coordinate standing for his European base.
stops.campa: Five months before the German army crosses into Poland he writes that there will be no war, that German insolence will shortly subside, that Italy will make friends with the British, and that the Arabs and their kings will lose the little market value they were supposed to have. He is the man credited afterward with having seen the catastrophe coming. In March 1939 he does not see it. The passage survives only as a bracketed excerpt in a magazine printed decades later, which names no original outlet.
stops.quote: [T]here will be no war; the German insolence will soon subside; Italy will make friends with the British and the Arabs, together with their kings, will lose even the little bit of market value they were supposed to have possessed until now.
stops.quote_source: Jabotinsky, March 1939, quoted in Jewish Review of Books, 'Confusion and Illusions, 1939'; the original outlet is not named there

stops.name: New York, the Jewish army
stops.date_confidence: attested that he traveled to the United States in 1940 to mobilize support for the NZO and a Jewish army, and offered Churchill a 130,000-strong volunteer corps on 12 May 1940 (Wikipedia); whether that offer was made in person or by letter, and from which city, is not established. Month set to March to order the segment. Benzion Netanyahu's secretaryship is stated in benjamin_netanyahu.journey.json and is not dated or placed by this pool.
stops.campa: He crosses to the United States to raise an army: a Jewish fighting force inside the Allied order of battle, recruited from Palestine and from the free countries, under its own flag. In May he puts a figure to Churchill, a hundred and thirty thousand volunteers. The American Jewish organizations are cool and the State Department is colder, and he works the halls and the mailing lists at fifty-nine with a bad heart. Serving as his secretary in these months is a young historian named Benzion Netanyahu.
stops.quote: In this war the Jewish people should count as one of the Allied nations.
stops.quote_source: Jabotinsky, The War and the Jew (New York: Altalena Press, 1942), published after his death

stops.name: Hunter, New York, the camp in the Catskills
stops.date_confidence: the civil date is contested and is NOT resolved by the JTA wire, which was published 5 August and says he died shortly before midnight last night, pointing to the night of 4 August. English Wikipedia gives 3 August; Encyclopaedia Judaica gives 4 August. The reconciliation is the Hebrew day: 29 Tammuz 5700 equals 4 August 1940, a day that begins at sunset on 3 August. Coordinates are the town of Hunter, not the camp site.
stops.campa: He drives up into the Catskills to inspect a Betar summer camp at Hunter, where American boys are drilling in the uniform his Riga schoolboys invented seventeen years earlier. He reviews the formation. During the evening he collapses, and dies of coronary thrombosis shortly before midnight, aged fifty-nine. The wire report calls him Vladimir Jabotinsky and puts the death shortly before midnight on the fourth. Wikipedia gives the third; Encyclopaedia Judaica the fourth; the Hebrew date kept by Israeli commemoration, 29 Tammuz, begins at sunset on the third.
suggested_refs: JTA archive obituary, 5 August 1940, jta.org/archive/vladimir-jabotinsky-dies-of-heart-attack-at-59-was-visiting-youth-camp

stops.name: Pinelawn, the grave at New Montefiore
stops.date_confidence: burial at New Montefiore Cemetery is attested (Wikipedia); the day is not, and is defaulted. Coordinates are English Wikipedia's for the cemetery, which is physically in Pinelawn with a Farmingdale postal address; both the geography and afterlife lenses supplied different and wrong pairs, reconciled here. The will's date of 3 November 1935, its terms, and Johanna's 1949 death could not be confirmed by any page reachable in this pass.
stops.campa: He is buried on Long Island, in ground chosen for him by circumstance. His will had instructed that he be buried wherever he happened to die, and that his remains be moved to the Land of Israel only by order of a future Jewish government: a sentence written by a man who assumed there would be a government and did not assume it would want him. Johanna is laid beside him in 1949. Ben-Gurion, prime minister of the state that by then exists, refuses for fifteen years to give the order, on the grounds that the country needs living Jews and not bones.

stops.name: Jerusalem, Mount Herzl
stops.date_confidence: the reburial on Mount Herzl by order of Levi Eshkol's government is attested (Wikipedia), which also supplies the coordinate 31 46 26 N, 35 10 50 E. The precise date of 9 July 1964, the cabinet approval of 15 March, and the ceremonies in New York, Paris, and Tel Aviv carry the dossier's sourcing only. The commemoration figures (57 streets and squares, the 2021 Odesa mural, the 2022 Kyiv street) come from English Wikipedia's legacy section, except the mural, which is a dossier claim that could not be confirmed.
stops.campa: Levi Eshkol's cabinet gives the order in March, and on the ninth of July the coffins of Ze'ev and Johanna Jabotinsky are lowered on Mount Herzl, a short walk from the grave of the man he saw once, in a hall in Basel, in 1903. The state that carries him up the hill is governed by his opponents. Fifty-seven streets and squares in Israel now bear his name, more than any other person's; Odesa put his young face on a wall in 2021, and Kyiv gave him a street in 2022, under the Ukrainian form of the name.
